title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy of Music on 1972-03-27
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: Crisp sound‑board capture of a high‑energy March ’72 show – tight playing, standout Good Lovin’, Bertha, China Cat > I Know You Rider and El Paso.
ai_review.review: The Miller transfer delivers an excellent, crystal‑clear soundboard that showcases Kreutzmann’s punchy drums and Jerry’s soaring vocals. Musically the concert is upbeat and danceable, with tight ensemble work and memorable moments on Good Lovin’, Bertha, Mr. Charlie and a spirited El Paso, even if it lacks the long jam sequences of other ’72 dates.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars, praising superb soundboard quality and high energy despite noting a lack of extended jams; weighted average yields ~4.3.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as crisp, clean, and 'superb' with an amazing mix; Kreutzmann's drums highlighted, no reported drop‑outs or muffling.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows smoothly with a bright, upbeat first set and a solid second; lacks long jam sequences but maintains high momentum throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his 'twanger' guitar tone and powerful vocals (over‑powering mic on Bertha), plus quirky banter and occasional octave transpositions.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for lively vocal contributions, jokes in the mix, and strong moxy on newer tunes like B.E. Woman.
band_member_comments.Keys: Briefly mentioned with a 'dragging' comment during Shuffle; overall keyboard work considered solid.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Kreutzmann’s drumming singled out as especially crisp and driving.
